output.scope_note: Not a benefit projection and not tax advice. The Social Security term is a flagged linearisation (ART761_SS_ESTIMATE_MODELED), not the SSA AIME formula - use art-282-social-security-claiming-optimizer or pf-139-social-security-bridge for a real benefit estimate. The career-setback compounding rate, the caregiving-year divisor, the 15 percent cap and the 20-year draw are modelling constants carried from the source, each UNGROUNDED. marginal_tax_rate_pct is accepted and echoed but enters no formula (source DIFFERS-D4: the Apex page reads it and never uses it). No inflation, no FMLA/state leave value, no unpaid-care opportunity cost beyond the direct wage loss, no employer-benefit valuation.
strategies: Max IRA/401(k) during and after the caregiving period - even small contributions compound over the years left to retirement
Consider spousal IRA contributions where applicable (allows retirement savings with little or no own income)
Negotiate phased re-entry or remote arrangements to limit the career setback
A written caregiver agreement with family for shared caregiving can provide modest taxable income and keep the Social Security record alive
Review employer EAP, FMLA and caregiver benefits BEFORE reducing hours
Invest in a credential or certification during or after caregiving to offset the 10% setback (see the AINumbers workforce ROI node)
